slice: Reject opposite-sign zero list expansion for constant floating IN
decision: Reject the candidate. Keep the accepted constant-list patch unchanged; do not add this patch to the optional runtime sequence. Short and nullable lists regress substantially in both balanced measurement series.
scope: Rust planner experiment for direct Float32/Float64 columns and recognized numeric constants containing zero but no NaN. Add the opposite zero sign and skip normalization. Retain the old path for computed zero-list operands, NaN constants, dynamic lists and unknown expressions; preserve required type widening.

correctness.note: The existing corpus uses the recorded Spark references and accepted after-captures. New edge queries are baseline-equivalence checks, not new Spark-reference runs. Computed operand controls additionally have independent expected rows. Native kernels are unchanged and their unit tests were not rerun.

performance.method: Release SQL benchmark, CPU 2, 1048576 input rows in 128 batches of 8192, one partition. Four fresh processes per variant in balanced order, two warmups and nine samples per process; report the median of process medians. Planning and execution counter phases are separate. All six perf events are fully scheduled. Instruction counts are totals across the gated phase (nine samples plus control handshake), not per query. No builds, correctness suites or other benchmark processes ran concurrently.

excluded_attempt.reason: The first repeat driver divided by zero when entering its empty planning selection, after completing the first eight execution processes. Excluded the whole partial series and reran the full balanced repeat with execution-only iteration.

performance.legacy_timing_not_run: The 112 old captures, including their plans, are unchanged. A prepared legacy timing driver was not run after the new workload regressions established rejection.

limitations: This is a rejected candidate, not a fix or a newly introduced regression in the accepted runtime.
The large three-to-four-entry regressions cross the existing local short-float dispatch threshold; they are not evidence that upstream DataFusion universally uses this threshold.
Single-item plans add a second comparison and OR. Equal result semantics and removing one normalization pass do not imply less execution work.
Long-list results cover 128 constants and a 97-value input domain with mostly matches. They do not justify a new list-length heuristic or an all-selectivity performance claim.
The DOUBLE zero_wide label has the same SQL and data as zero_short. Its two ANSI captures are repeats, not additional distinct compatibility coverage.
Planning and execution measurements exclude Delta I/O and are not combined request latency. Results come from one machine and core.

No new Spark reference run was needed for this baseline-preservation experiment. Existing raw Spark differences, fallback normalization costs and small historical timing differences remain unresolved.

    if record['existed']:

        allowed.add(record['sha256'])
    if file.exists(): assert sha(file) in allowed, key
    else: assert not record['existed'], key
for key, record in executables.items():
    allowed = {record['sha256']} | {sha(p / f'{v}-{key}') for v in ['before', 'after'] if (p / f'{v}-{key}').exists()}

canonical = {v: {r['id']: r for r in load(p / f'{v}-check.json')['results']} for v in ['before', 'after']}
cases = [r['id'].removesuffix('_ansitrue') for r in canonical['before'].values() if r['ansi']]
planning = ['generic_in_utf8_low', 'generic_in_utf8_long_list', 'generic_in_decimal_low',
            'generic_in_float_zero_single', 'generic_in_double_zero_single',
            'generic_in_float_zero_short', 'generic_in_double_zero_short',
            'generic_in_float_zero_long_list', 'generic_in_double_zero_long_list',
            'generic_in_float_zero_nullable', 'generic_in_double_zero_nullable',
            'generic_in_float_zero_wide', 'generic_in_double_nan_short']
env = os.environ.copy()
assert not any(k.startswith(('MALLOC_', 'GLIBC_', 'LD_PRELOAD', 'DECIMAL_BENCH_')) for k in env)
order = ['before', 'after', 'after', 'before', 'after', 'before', 'before', 'after']
runs = []
for index, variant in enumerate(order):
    for phase, selected in [('execution', cases), ('planning', planning)]:
        shift = index % len(selected)
        for case in selected[shift:] + selected[:shift]:
            directory = out / f'{index}-{variant}-{phase}-{case}'
            directory.mkdir()
            for name in ['control', 'ack']: os.mkfifo(directory / name)
            command = ['perf', 'stat', '--delay=-1', f'--control=fifo:{directory}/control,{directory}/ack',
                       '--json-output', '-o', str(directory / 'counters.jsonl'), '-e',
                       '{instructions:u,cycles:u},task-clock:u,context-switches:u,cpu-migrations:u,page-faults:u',
                       '--', 'taskset', '-c', '2', str(p / f'{variant}-bench'),
                       str(directory / 'capture.json'), 'generic-in', case]
            result = subprocess.run(command, env=env | {'DECIMAL_BENCH_PERF_DIR': str(directory),
                                    'DECIMAL_BENCH_PERF_PHASE': phase}, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                    check=True, timeout=180)
            capture = load(directory / 'capture.json')
            assert len(capture['results']) == 2
            for row in capture['results']:
                assert {k: v for k, v in row.items() if k not in ['samples_ms', 'planning_samples_ms']} == canonical[variant][row['id']]
            timed = next(r for r in capture['results'] if r['ansi'])
            assert len(timed['samples_ms']) == len(timed['planning_samples_ms']) == 9
            counters = [json.loads(line) for line in (directory / 'counters.jsonl').read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith('{')]
            assert len(counters) == 6 and all(c['pcnt-running'] == 100 for c in counters)
            assert result.stderr.count('Events enabled') == 1
            runs.append({'variant': variant, 'index': index, 'phase': phase, 'case': case,
                         'command': command, 'planning_samples_ms': timed['planning_samples_ms'],
                         'samples_ms': timed['samples_ms'], 'counters': counters})
    (p / 'generic-performance.json').write_text(json.dumps({'order': order, 'cases': cases, 'planning': planning, 'runs': runs}, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(index, variant, 'complete', flush=True)

summary = {}
for phase, selected in [('execution', cases), ('planning', planning)]:
    summary[phase] = {}
    for case in selected:
        groups = {}
        for variant in ['before', 'after']:
            rows = [r for r in runs if r['variant'] == variant and r['case'] == case and r['phase'] == phase]
            assert len(rows) == 4
            medians = [statistics.median(r['planning_samples_ms' if phase == 'planning' else 'samples_ms']) for r in rows]
            instructions = [next(float(c['counter-value']) for c in r['counters'] if c['event'] == 'instructions:u') for r in rows]
            groups[variant] = {'process_medians_ms': medians, 'median_ms': statistics.median(medians),
                               'process_instructions': instructions, 'median_instructions': statistics.median(instructions)}
        summary[phase][case] = groups | {
            'latency_change_pct': 100 * (groups['after']['median_ms'] / groups['before']['median_ms'] - 1),
            'instruction_change_pct': 100 * (groups['after']['median_instructions'] / groups['before']['median_instructions'] - 1)}
(p / 'generic-summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + '\n')
for phase, rows in summary.items():
    for case, row in rows.items():
        print(phase, case, round(row['latency_change_pct'], 2), round(row['instruction_change_pct'], 2), flush=True)
